source.citation: Wikipedia, History of Cameroon (CC BY-SA 4.0), and the UNHCR Refworld timeline. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.summary: Germany declared a protectorate over much of present-day Cameroon, which became the colony of Kamerun. Britain recognised it in 1886 and France in 1885. The capital was first Buea and later Yaoundé.
attributes.note: One source says July 1884 without a day.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Kamerun (CC BY-SA 4.0), and an article in History in Africa on the national archives of Cameroon. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

content.name: Kamerun campaign of the First World War

attributes.summary: French, British and Belgian forces invaded German Kamerun in 1914 and occupied it. The German army surrendered in 1916.

source.citation: Wikipedia, History of Cameroon (CC BY-SA 4.0), and GlobalSecurity.org, Cameroon history. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

content.name: League of Nations mandates over Cameroon

attributes.summary: After Germany's defeat, the territory was split into two League of Nations Class B mandates. France administered the larger eastern part (French Cameroun) and Britain administered Northern and Southern Cameroons.

source.citation: Britannica, History of Cameroon, and Wikimedia Commons map notes on Cameroon boundary changes. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

content.name: United Nations trusteeships replace the mandates

attributes.summary: The League of Nations mandates became United Nations trust territories. French Cameroun became a trust territory on 13 December 1946.

source.citation: UNHCR Refworld timeline on Cameroon. Another source gives 1947 as the founding year. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

content.name: Union des Populations du Cameroun (UPC) founded

attributes.summary: A nationalist party that opposed French rule and campaigned for the reunification of East and West Cameroon. It grew more active through the 1950s.
